card.name: Route words after administer or flow
card.fires_on: Small linking or route words such as via, in, down, either or gastric that come right after a verb of giving, flowing or connecting. The next word is expected to name a channel, such as a line, tube, pump or device.

modes.label: Route of giving
modes.description: The word via or a route word follows administer, or comes right before a tube or line.
modes.example: Only administer AFREZZA<< via>> oral inhalation using the AFREZZ

modes.label: Linking word before a channel
modes.description: A preposition or adverb after a verb of flowing, connecting or entering, before a place or path.
modes.example: It is like the dew of Hermon, which flows<< down>> upon the hills of Zion”

modes.label: Verb after blood products
modes.description: The verb administered in text about separate intravenous lines.
modes.example: blood products and sodium nitrite can be<< administered>> simultaneously using separate intravenous lines

card.writes: It pushes toward unusual word pieces and away from stream, stdin and pipe words, so it adds no clear output effect.
card.plain: It marks the small word that introduces how or through what something is given or connected, such as via a tube or line.
